lines.zh: 六条腿踩着浅滩的软泥
lines.en: Six legs tread the soft mud of the shallows.
My long snout probes the water.
A skirt of membrane drapes my tail.
I slip between the reeds.

lines.zh: 长吻在水面划出一道线
lines.en: My snout draws a line on the water.
Six feet squelch through the mud.
I walk along the water's edge.
My tail trails like wet cloth.
I lower my head for movement in the water.
I skirt the deeper hollows.
I move steadily, step by step.
The membrane on my back gleams faintly.
I rest my long snout on the surface.
All six legs have sunk into the mud.
My tail membrane sways gently.
I watch a fleck of light in the water.
I open my jaws and let the water pass.
Only insects are singing around me.
For once, I am not moving.
Drops of water bead on my snout.
I breathe slowly.
A little mud slumps by my feet.
I listen to the reeds.
My tail membrane pushes the water aside.
This pool is shallow.
I settle down in the mud.
My long snout rises slowly.
You are standing at the water's edge.

lines.zh: 你看得出我的吻有多长吗
lines.en: Can you tell how long my snout is?
None of my six legs moved.
I watch you in the reflection.
You have muddied all the water.
I can see your feet under the water.
I turn my snout slowly aside.

lines.zh: 水声把你的位置告诉我了
lines.en: The water told me where you stand.
Six legs, slow strides — no hurry.

lines.zh: 我歪头,让吻尖离你远点
lines.en: I tilt my head to angle my snout away.
You are standing on my waterline.
My long snout twists.
My six legs slide in the mud.
My tail membrane is yanked.
I retreat back into the water.
That struck my neck.
The tip of my snout has split.
I sink a little into the mud.
The water will feel better.
I can still bite.
I steady myself slowly.
A scent drifts through the water.
My snout turns that way.
My six legs start moving.
Something washed clean smells best.
This is still dripping.
I probe my snout closer.

lines.zh: 水里跟着的味道更清楚
lines.en: In water the scent is clearer.
Do not pull your hand back yet.

lines.zh: 长吻微张，我闻到水里的肉。
lines.en: My long snout parts; I smell meat in the water.
Lower it a little more.
You bumped my long snout.
I turn my head to shed the force.

lines.zh: 六条腿在泥里滑了一下
lines.en: My six legs slip in the mud.
My tail caught you.
You stepped on one of my six legs.
We have churned the mud.

lines.zh: 我的尾鳍扫过你，湿漉漉的。
lines.en: My tail fin sweeps past you, dripping.
Water splashes over us both.
Do not walk against my snout.
Steady; this mud is slippery.
I bring my snout to yours.
Our six legs sink side by side.
Our tail membranes touch.
This shallows is enough for us.
The water will hide our scent.

lines.zh: 我们一起往芦苇深处走
lines.en: We head deeper into the reeds.
No hurry; the water is always here.
You dive; I keep watch.
Quiet now; do not scare the fish.

lines.zh: 尾鳍碰尾鳍，这片水够安静。
lines.en: Fin against fin; this water is quiet enough.
My snout flicks it up.
I hold it and swallow slowly.
It is slicker in the water.
Too hard; I give up.
I press it down with a foreclaw.
It slipped off my snout.
This does not belong in the water.
I hold it in my jaws for now.
There are more in the mud.
I will take all of these.
The movement in the water is you.
My snout is aimed.
I flatten low against the water.
Six legs spread to both sides.
Shallow water favours me.
The mud where you stand is soft.
I can hear your footsteps.

lines.zh: 我的长吻一开，水就空了。
lines.en: My long snout opens and the water empties.
I wait for the ripples to settle.
Retreat, and the mud will hold you.
This pool is mine.
My whole body is taut.
Then let it start now.
Whatever you do, do not look back.
I follow the ripples.
Every step you take, I know.
I circle behind the reeds.
My snout stays pointed at you.
Beneath, my tail is paddling.
You have reached firmer ground.
That works badly against me.
I will wait a while more.
You are looking somewhere else.
This angle will do.
I close two more steps.
The water covers my sound.
You have turned around.
Then there is no more pretending.
I lower my snout tip.
My long snout snaps out.
Fine teeth clamp on your arm.
I whip my head and pull you off balance.
Six legs brace in the mud.
My tail membrane slaps your leg.
Water sprays high.
I bite twice.
I step back and aim again.
The snout tip arrived first.
You are dragged into the shallows.
Blood darkens the water.
I let go and shake my snout.
I bite once more.
That is quite enough.
The reeds move first.
My long snout comes out of the weeds.
Six feet settle into the mud.
My tail membrane spreads on the water.
One more shadow in the pool.
I raise my head, snout dripping.
My prints come in three pairs.
I have stirred the shallows.
I shift toward the bank.
These reeds are cover enough.
I make a low sound.
The surface has gone flat again.
I plant myself in the mud.
I am here, and no one saw.
Do not linger at the water's edge.
This pool has a master.

lines.zh: 水被烧热,尾巴的膜缩起来
lines.en: The water heats; my tail membrane curls.
I land hard on the muddy bank.

lines.zh: 我在水里反而喘不上气
lines.en: In the water, I cannot draw breath.
Mud and water erupt together.

lines.zh: 一根尖东西擦过我的吻
lines.en: Something sharp grazes my snout.

lines.zh: 那股力量让我的膜发烫
lines.en: That force heats my membrane.
Hunger makes my snout tip tremble.
Lightning crawls up through the water to me.
No water here, and no mud.
